definition: Quell means to put down or calm a disturbance by force or authority.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word quell. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know quell should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Two senior stewards moved through the grandstand to quell the scuffle before it could spread beyond one row.
Calming a crowd is gentler than quelling it — soothing words and patience, with no force or authority behind them.
Crushing goes even further than quelling — a quelled disturbance is over, but a crushed one is destroyed so thoroughly that nothing dares stir again.

To subdue is to bring a person or group under control by force — the rioters, the intruder, the crowd itself are wrestled down. Quell points at the disturbance rather than the people: an uproar, a mutiny, a wave of fear put down by someone with authority. You subdue the mob; you quell the riot.

To quash is to stamp something out decisively with official power — an indictment, a subpoena, a proposed rule can all be quashed by whoever has the authority to kill it on paper. Quell belongs to live disturbances: riots, mutinies, panics put down while they are still moving. Quash ends measures; quell ends trouble.

Cwellan left no other common English word behind. Scholars suspect a family tie to the everyday word for ending a life, but the spellings drifted so far apart over the centuries that nothing visible connects them now — quell stands alone.
Quell means to put down or calm a disturbance by force or authority.
It took the head zookeeper four minutes to quell the chaos in the aviary — nets lowered, lights dimmed, one recorded owl call — before a single feather was harmed.
Quell is not gentle soothing: it comes with force or authority behind it.
Disturbances are quelled from above — an uproar, a mutiny, a wave of fear — by someone with the standing to put them down.
Quell pairs an authority with a disturbance: guards quell riots, captains quell mutinies, statements quell rumors and fears.
Use 'calm' or 'settle' when there's no force in play, and quash — its chip on this card — when what's being killed is official, like a ruling or an indictment.
In this unit's family, quell handles trouble already burning, while forestall stops it from ever igniting.
